proposals.description: Retain two supported filtration aliases and make two inherited insufficiently scoped aliases nonresolving, after actual source reconstruction. Final-review qualification of the historical #260 dilution rationale: the original CCAP PE footnote explicitly says to filter natural seawater, reduce it to 95% using glass distilled water, and autoclave. That prepared input is then dosed at 950 cm3; the prior dilution is not inferred from the receiving-medium dose. The literal 95%-strength label is retained as REJECTED_LABEL on this bare filtered-seawater owner, without inventing the percentage basis, final volume, component ratio or a new preparation owner. The unqualified Natural seawater alias is also nonresolving: its recovered JCM1377 contexts state natural seawater without filtration. Supported Filtered natural seawater and Natural seawater (filtrated) aliases remain. Earlier #260 mapping evidence and histories are preserved as historical rationale, superseded only on these alias applicability points by this source-backed qualification. The two assigned filtered cases are not reinterpreted as the 95% preparation. Sources: https://www.ccap.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/MR_PE.pdf ; https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1377 .

This class is distinct from source-disjunctive filtered-aged-water OR DaigoSP choices in 38/116.

proposals.description: NBRC 15/16/22/24/1071 source inputs retain a 2% salinity qualifier. Cases 101/105 support only a common salinity-qualified material class; neither absence of stated origin nor equal salinity proves shared chemical composition or a shared preparation. This isolated class proposal makes no resolved source-to-owner binding and no selection of natural versus artificial preparation. No pure NaCl concentration or artificial formula is inferred. Case 22 explicitly offers alternative preparations and retains its branch-choice hold.
